newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-BENFICA WINS BUT PORTO KEEPS UP PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENFICA WINS BUT PORTO KEEPS UP PRESSURE.

text.p: LISBON, Oct 21 - Leaders Benfica and second-placed Porto had home wins on Monday to strengthen their grip on the Portuguese league.
Benfica captain Joao Pinto put the Lisbon side in front after just three minutes against Estrela da Amadora and Brazilian striker Osmar Donizete added a second 10 minutes from time.
Donizete, who was called up for the Brazilian national squad last week, is joint top-scorer in the Portuguese league with Setubal's Chiquinho Conde. Both have six goals.
Although he did not score, Swedish striker Martin Pringle made a fine debut for Benfica, laying on the pass for the first goal.
After a inspired start, Porto had to struggle for their 1-0 win over local rivals Boavista who attacked strongly in the second half.
Slovene striker Zlatko headed Porto into the lead in the 27th minute after a cross from the left by defender Fernando Mendes.

Boavista midfielder Sergio Duarte was sent off for arguing with the referee over the validity of the goal. Shortly after the start of the second half, Porto were also reduced to 10 men after Jose Barroso was sent off for his second bookable offence.
As Boavista pressed forward in search of an equaliser, Porto were grateful for the splendid form of goalkeeper Henrique Hilario who denied the visitors a goal with a series of fine saves.
Benfica lead the league with 19 points, two more than Porto. Sporting are one point further behind, in third place.
